rows.source_support: OutboundService.sendInitial's claim callback evaluates validateDispatchContext, including the trusted text window and credential version, before currentActorHasGrant executes FOR SHARE OF u, r, b. That authorization query can block. After it returns, claimInitial rechecks database time against only leaseExpiresAt and commits SENDING without reevaluating the window or credential tuple. A trusted window can expire during the wait while the 90-second lease remains live, allowing an official text POST outside the approved window. A credential-version change during the same interval also lacks a pinned credential row or final recheck. This violates D02/D04/D06 at the durable claim boundary. The existing expiry/revocation tests exercise other orderings; the embedded evidence does not demonstrate this ordering. Exploitability is source-supported and unexecuted here; the blast radius is an initial outbound operation in an authorized BU.

rows.source_support: InitialMessageService.options requests the latest 11 intents by createdAt/id for a conversation and BU. The supplied intent indexes do not support that ordering: the conversation index places slotReleasedAt and state before createdAt and omits the id tie-breaker. Consequently, LIMIT 11 bounds returned rows while PostgreSQL must examine and sort the conversation's accumulated attempt history. Released attempts are retained, so this work grows over time. Active ordinary-admission listing has a similar ordering mismatch when many tokens remain unreleased. The embedded EPS evidence covers inbox ordering, message existence and trusted-window projections, without a plan for these new recovery-history queries. This is a source/schema-supported access-path gap, without a measured outage claim.

rows.source_support: Initial claim and accepted local completion hold provider_resource_identities FOR SHARE before currentActorHasGrant requests shared locks on user, grant and BU rows. The preserved TemplateObservationService.ownsLease takes user/BU/grant/channel FOR UPDATE before requesting that same identity FOR UPDATE. A concurrent refresh can therefore hold the BU/user lock while waiting for the identity, as the initial transaction holds the identity while waiting for the BU/user lock. PostgreSQL must abort a participant. During accepted local completion this can unnecessarily leave a confirmed external send locally blocked. The cycle is directly supported by both embedded owners; its occurrence was not reproduced in this review. The blast radius is concurrent refresh and initial dispatch/completion for the shared official resource.
